profile.name: Jesse Chen
profile.headline: Building technology that solves real problems for real people
profile.claim: Secure mobile, AI, and full-stack systems.
profile.description: Computer science student at Carnegie Mellon building secure mobile, AI, and full-stack systems that solve real problems.

experiences.summary: Shipped Android features for 500K+ members, improved billing and payments flows, fixed production defects, and built a security-audit pipeline validating authentication across 220+ API endpoints.

Launched a campus AI platform that grounds every answer in live university data via MCP tools, deterministically blocks hallucinated claims, and streams first tokens at 1.5s p95, spanning a LangGraph/FastAPI agent and React client. Built injection-hardened cross-chat memory with LLM fact extraction, pgvector dedup, and per-user isolation.

Overhauled a 10K+ user Flutter app's main flows from founder spec to release. Shipped skin-tone shade matching, engineering a perceptual color engine (sRGB to CIELAB, Delta-E) and the live gauge it powers, pinpointing the user's tone and confidence band on a shade spectrum. Cut homepage load time ~75% via API fan-out, feed prefetching, token pagination, and TTL-cached revisits.

Built the geospatial ETL pipeline powering CMU's campus navigation site for 700+ monthly users, parsing 15K+ OpenStreetMap nodes and ArcGIS facility records into footprints, floors, and entrances for 74 buildings.

experiences.summary: Built Unreal Engine 5 Blueprint gameplay systems for grappling, tethering, and local multiplayer combat, synchronizing physics-driven interactions, collision feedback, and elimination state in real time.
Designed and taught project-based Python, C++, and JavaScript curriculum centered on algorithms and competitive problem solving through structured implementation labs.

Developed and evaluated a computer-vision model for Parkinson's exercise-form assessment, achieving 95.4% mean accuracy in controlled video trials, and co-authored a peer-reviewed paper presented at CS & IT-CSCP 2024.

projects.name: ParkiWell
projects.lead: An offline-first Flutter care platform for Parkinson’s patients, pairing a real-time computer-vision exercise coach with crash-proof, encrypted health-data sync.
bullets: Engineered a MediaPipe 3D-pose coach that counts, scores, and speaks cues for every rep, running on-device from camera frame to feedback in under 10 ms.
Built an encrypted write journal replayed exactly once via idempotent PostgreSQL RPC, surviving 1M fault-injected writes and 100 process kills with zero loss.

caseStudy.challenge: Care tracking cannot become unavailable when connectivity drops, and reconnecting must never duplicate or erase health records. Exercise guidance also has to react in real time, on-device, without sending video anywhere.
approach: Recorded offline mutations in an encrypted write journal replayed exactly once via idempotent PostgreSQL RPC.
Tracked 3D pose with MediaPipe to count, score, and speak cues for every rep of guided exercises.
Protected every hosted table with row-level security and shipped signed builds through CI/CD.
outcomes: Zero data loss across 100 process kills

projects.name: Agoriai
projects.lead: An anonymous student career network built in 36 hours at TartanHacks 2026: a React 19 client, a 36-endpoint Bun/Elysia REST API over a 13-table PostgreSQL schema, and privacy controls enforced at the server boundary.
bullets: Designed a server-enforced four-tier identity privacy system with DM-based mutual reveal, applied to every serialized API response.
Built a D3 force-directed relationship graph plus an evasion-resistant moderation engine with leetspeak normalization and fuzzy matching.

caseStudy.challenge: Career networks are useful only when students can discover relevant peers without exposing private identity or academic context. The system needed to preserve anonymity while still supporting search, discussion, and relationship exploration.
approach: Enforced four identity-visibility tiers on the server rather than trusting the client.
Modeled student-company relationships as weighted edges and rendered them through a D3 force-directed graph.
Normalized leetspeak and applied fuzzy matching before moderation decisions.

projects.name: Tarocchi
projects.lead: An interactive tarot narrative web experience with five illustrated scene branches, spread-based card readings interpreted by Claude, replayable state-driven progression, parallax, and synchronized audio.
bullets: Modeled route and scene state explicitly so branching flows remain coherent as narrative complexity grows.
Built a reusable presentation pipeline for animated transitions, layered parallax, and synchronized sound.

caseStudy.challenge: Branching story scenes had to feel cinematic without allowing animation, audio, and route state to drift apart, and card readings needed to respond to the player's actual choices.
approach: Represented narrative progress as explicit state instead of coupling it to visual components.
Synchronized scene transitions and audio cues from the same route events.
Fed the chosen spread, cards, and scene into a Claude-backed generator for personalized readings.

projects.name: MyCommunity
projects.lead: A native Java Android platform for Boy Scouts troop discovery with live Firebase data, Google Maps, runtime location permissions, and Google Sign-In.
bullets: Bound Firebase realtime listeners to live map markers with auto-zoom bounds and runtime location permissions.
Integrated four external APIs (Google Maps, Firebase, Google Sign-In, NYT Top Stories) with async OkHttp, Gson parsing, and Glide caching.
terminal: nyt api ▸ feed cached via glide

caseStudy.challenge: Troop discovery data had to stay current on a location-aware map while respecting Android’s authentication and runtime permission model.
approach: Bound Firebase listeners to map marker lifecycle and profile state.
Handled location permission and Google Sign-In as explicit application states.
Fetched community news asynchronously and cached images for responsive browsing.
